query: What comparator selection criteria and statistical methods (e.g., propensity scores, interrupted time series) will we use when randomized designs are infeasible?

response.query: What comparator selection criteria and statistical methods (e.g., propensity scores, interrupted time series) will we use when randomized designs are infeasible?
response.answer: When randomized designs are infeasible, propensity score matching and interrupted time series analysis are commonly used. Propensity scores help control for confounding variables, while interrupted time series assesses changes over time.
